title: Fast/Slow Pointer Relationship
summary: Move two pointers through the same linked or indexed path at different rates or with a fixed gap so their relative positions reveal structure.
recognition_signals: each state has one next state or one linear successor
the problem asks about a midpoint, cycle, or fixed distance
core_rules: The useful information is the relationship between pointer positions, not a history of all visited positions.
Pointer movement must preserve the intended rate or gap.
structural_steps: initialize the pointers according to the desired relationship
advance them at their defined rates
test the relationship after each movement
stop when the relationship proves the requested property

common_confusions.distinction: Fast/slow pointers follow the same successor path with a rate or gap relationship. Opposing pointers reason from two ordered boundaries.
